svg.title: Lumentree Local security model
svg.desc: Diagram showing that the server mediates between ESP32 and Home Assistant and that Device ID alone is not enough for protected read access.
svg.text: Current Security Model
The ESP32 and Home Assistant do not trust each other directly. The API server mediates claim, read access, and optional write access.
ESP32 bridge
Uploads telemetry
Reports gateway status
Registers read and write pairing tokens
ESP32 uses the backend server API token.
API server
Binds gateway_id + Device ID + MAC
Validates read pairing token claims
Validates write pairing token claims
Issues long-lived read and write grants
Protected read endpoints now require a grant or the server token.
Home Assistant
Claims read access with Device ID + read token
Optionally claims write access with write token
Uses grant tokens for normal polling and writes
Home Assistant does not need the backend server master token.
What Device ID alone does not do
Device ID alone is no longer enough for protected read access to normal device endpoints.
A new user still needs a valid read pairing token from the ESP32 local portal.
Write access remains separate and optional.
The server can reject claims when the gateway is offline, mismatched, or expired.
Result: normal telemetry is protected, and direct inverter control needs an additional grant.
